raw_text:
Here is a consolidated, printer-friendly 12-week couch-to-5K plan with integrated strength work, explicit interval training, a tempo run day, a Parkrun/test option in Week 8, a finisher/race-day prep week, and an asthmatic safety framework. The plan uses a 3-run-per-week structure (A, B, C), plus 2 weekly strength days (S1, S2). Tempo runs and intervals are phased to build toward a 5K readiness while accommodating exercise-induced asthma (EIA). Week 12 includes a dedicated finisher/race-day prep micro-cycle followed by a taper, per your request.

Legend
- A: Main run with intervals or progression
- B: Easy run or cross-training
- C: Technique/shorter interval day
- T: Tempo run day
- S1: Strength Day A
- S2: Strength Day B
- Parkrun: Optional 5K test in Week 8 (Parkrun day) or Week 12a as noted
- Notes in parentheses provide pacing targets or reminders

Safety and EIA reminders (applies to all weeks)
- Carry and know how to use the SABA inhaler; use 10–15 minutes prior to exertion if prescribed.
- Dynamic warm-up 10 minutes before every run; include mobility and thoracic breathing drills.
- For cold air, indoor options or pre-warm air; consider a scarf/mask to pre-warm.
- If symptoms occur, stop, use inhaler, reassess; seek medical advice if symptoms persist beyond 15–20 minutes after inhaler use.
- Hydration, sleep, and nutrition support performance and recovery.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — base with gentle intervals; strength integrated
Week 1
- A: 10-minute warm-up; 1 min jog / 2 min walk x 8; 5–7 minute cooldown
- B: Cross-train 20–30 minutes
- C: Easy run: 1 min jog / 2 min walk x 6
- S1: 2 sets
  - Goblet squat 8–10
  - Romanian deadlift (hip hinge) 8–10
  - Glute bridges 10–12
  - Calf raises 12–15
  - Plank 30 seconds
- Tempo Day: none

Week 2
- A: 2 min jog / 2 min walk x 6
- B: Cross-train 25–35 minutes
- C: 2 min jog / 1 min walk x 8
- S1: 3 sets if ready; add light weight if form ok
- Tempo Day: none

Week 3
- A: 3 min jog / 1.5 min walk x 6
- B: Mobility day or light cardio
- C: 4 min jog / 2 min walk x 5
- S2: optional after B
- Tempo Day: none

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — tempo introduction, stronger body, interval density grows
Week 4
- A: 4 min jog / 1.5 min walk x 5
- B: Cross-train or easy run 25–35 minutes
- C: 5 min jog / 2 min walk x 4
- S1: 3 sets
- Tempo Day (T): 8–12 minutes tempo after 10-minute warm-up; 3–4 min easy recovery

Week 5
- A: 6 min jog / 2 min walk x 4
- B: S2 after B (optional): push-ups incline 3x8–12; rows 3x8–12; Pallof press 3x8 per side; farmer’s carry 3x30s
- C: 8 min jog / 1–2 min walk x 3
- S1: goblet squat progressions with light load
- Tempo Day (T): 9–12 minutes tempo

Week 6
- A: 8 min jog / 1.5 min walk x 3
- B: Cross-train 30 minutes
- C: 10 min jog / 2 min walk x 2
- S1/S2: load progression; consider small weight increase
- Tempo Day (T): 12 minutes tempo or two blocks of 6 minutes with 2–3 min easy between

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 — longer runs, tempo focus, interval expansion
Week 7
- A: 12 min jog / 2 min walk x 2; + 60–90s pickups x2 if tolerated
- B: S1 strength day
  - Goblet squats 3x10
  - Romanian deadlift 3x10
  - Lunges or split squats 3x8 per leg
  - Glute bridges 3x12
  - Calf raises 3x15
  - Plank 3x40s
- C: 15 min jog / 2 min walk + 4x30s strong pickups (2 min easy between)
- Tempo integration: tempo elements introduced progressively within C or as a separate block in B as tolerated

Week 8
- A: 18 min jog / 2 min walk + 2x5 min steady runs (tempo-like)
- B: S2 strength day
  - Push-ups or incline push-ups 3x10–12
  - Dumbbell rows 3x10–12
  - Pallof press 3x10 per side
  - Farmer’s carry 3x40s
  - Dead bug 3x10 per side
- C: Recovery run 12–14 min easy + 6–8 x 20s strides
- Parkrun test: Optional 5K test this week; if completed, use data to refine Weeks 9–12 pacing
- Tempo Day (T): 12–14 minutes tempo if feasible

Week 9
- A: 22–24 minutes continuous at a brisk tempo; 2–3 minutes easy after
- B: S1 strength day
  - Goblet squats 3x12
  - Hip thrusts 3x12
  - Step-ups 3x10 per leg
  - Calf raises 3x15
  - Band pull-aparts 3x12
  - Plank 3x40–45s
- C: Brisk run day with technique focus; 20 minutes continuous + 3x30s faster
- Tempo Day (T): 12–15 minutes tempo with shorter faster segments; aim for progressions toward race-pace feel

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 — peak speed, race-pace readiness, taper
Week 10
- A: 25 minutes continuous at aerobic pace; 3x3 minutes at tempo pace with 2 min easy between
- B: S2 strength day
- C: 15 minutes technique work + 4x60s at race pace with 2 min easy
- Tempo Day (T): 12–15 minutes tempo with 1–2 short surges if tolerated

Week 11
- A: 28 minutes continuous with 2x6 minutes near-race pace; 3 minutes easy
- B: S1 strength day
- C: Short run with 4x20–30s brisk; 2–3 minutes easy
- Tempo Day (T): 12–16 minutes tempo; maintain control

Week 12 — Finisher / Race-Day Prep Week (12a) + Week 12 taper
Week 12a (Finisher / Race-Day Prep)
- Day A: Short Tempo + Pace Tune
  - 10-minute warm-up
  - 8 minutes tempo (RPE 6–7) + 2 min easy
  - 4 minutes near race pace with 2 min easy
  - 5-minute cooldown
- Day B: Easy Run + Progression
  - 10-minute warm-up
  - 12–15 minutes easy, finish last 3–4 minutes brisk
  - 5-minute cooldown
- Day C: Parkrun Test or Time Trial (optional)
  - If Parkrun already done, replace with 20-minute easy run + 4x20s strides
  - If not done, perform a 5K time-trial at controlled effort: 20–25 minutes total, last 1–2 minutes at race-pace feel; cooldown 10 minutes
- Day T (Tempo) optional or merged with Day A: 12-minute tempo if scheduling allows
- S1: 2–3 x 8–10
- S2: 2 x 8–12 (optional)

Week 12 (Taper)
- A: 25–28 minutes easy to moderate; last 5 minutes at light race-pace feel
- B: Easy Recovery 20–30 minutes
- C: Mobility and activation; 15–20 minutes drills + gentle strides
- Race-day readiness check: optional 5K time-check at comfortable pace if feeling strong

Notes on Week 12 flow
- If you used Week 12a as a finisher/race-day prep, Week 12 becomes a traditional taper focusing on maintaining freshness and mental rehearsal.
- If you merged Week 12a into Week 12, you’ll have a single taper with lighter tempo work and a final, short race-pace block.

Parkrun integration options
- Week 8 Parkrun test (optional): Treat as a controlled-speed check rather than a full-out race; use inhaler as prescribed; note pace, EIA symptoms, and fueling.
- Week 12 Parkrun: If not done in Week 8, can be the final race-day practice under taper conditions.
- Always have a plan for fueling and breathing during Parkrun; post-Parkrun cooldown and mobility work.

Strength progression guidance
- Start with bodyweight; add light dumbbells/kettlebells only when technique and breathing are solid.
- Rest between sets mostly 60–90 seconds; circuit days may keep rest shorter but ensure breathing remains controlled.
- Focus on posterior chain (glutes, hamstrings, calves) and anti-extension core stability to support breathing mechanics and running economy.

Pacing and progression notes
- Early weeks: keep runs easy; RPE targets 3–4 during running segments.
- Mid phases: introduce tempo blocks (RPE 6–7) and shorter, controlled intervals to build leg turnover and pacing.
- Later weeks: emphasize race-pace readiness; include race-pace blocks of 3–6 minutes with appropriate recoveries.
- If asthma symptoms flare, scale back tempo and interval duration, revert to easier weeks, and reassess.

Testing and progression tracking
- Record weekly data: distance, duration, pace, RPE, EIA symptoms, inhaler use, and any walk breaks.
- Parkrun results (if completed) provide a practical feedback point to calibrate Weeks 9–12 pacing and tempo progression.
- After Week 12, adjust target 5K pace and set new progression milestones (e.g., 10K plan or 5K time improvements).
